BiblicalUsage: This word means to bend or crook — and in Scripture it is almost always moral bending, doing wrong. David says he has done wickedly when he counts the people, Daniel confesses we have sinned and committed iniquity, and God warns David's son that if he commits iniquity he will be chastened. The same root bends a bow and bends a heart off course.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is honest about what sin is: not a mistake but a bending away from what is straight. And I hold that the same God who chastens also forgives when we own the bend, the way Daniel and David did.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
